language.script_notes: Malay in Latin script with English widely used; Chinese and Tamil scripts appear on shopfront signage reflecting the peninsula's large Chinese and Indian communities.

road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles on the peninsula often carry black rectangular labels with white lettering — this black pole sticker distinguishes the peninsula from Borneo, where the stickers are white.

architecture.roof_style: Domed and minareted mosques everywhere; older wooden mosques with triple-tiered stilted roofs; colonial-era buildings in Kuala Lumpur and Georgetown blend Mughal, Tudor and neo-Gothic influences.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal and clay tile; domed concrete on mosques.
architecture.wall_construction: Terraced concrete shophouses and row houses dominate towns and cities; traditional Malay stilt houses in rural kampungs; Chinese clan houses and temples; the Petronas Twin Towers and KL Tower in Kuala Lumpur.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Pastel-painted terraces and shophouses; white and green on mosques.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colonial and Mughal-influenced civic buildings (Sultan Abdul Samad Building); the National Mosque; the Petronas Twin Towers; shophouse streetscapes in Georgetown and Malacca (UNESCO-listed); rubber and oil palm plantation estates.

nature.vegetation: Endless rows of oil palm and rubber trees blanket the lowlands — plantation monoculture is a defining peninsular tell; dense rainforest in the mountainous interior (Titiwangsa Range); mangroves along the west coast.
nature.terrain: A mountainous central spine (Titiwangsa Range, including the Cameron Highlands' tea plantations) flanked by flat coastal plains, with a heavily developed west coast (Kuala Lumpur–Penang corridor) and quieter east coast.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid tropical rainforest climate; highland areas (Cameron Highlands, Genting) are noticeably cooler and misty.

vehicles.plate_color: W prefix for Kuala Lumpur, and prefixes such as B (Selangor), P (Penang), J (Johor) identify state.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Perodua and Proton dominate — especially the Perodua Myvi, a hugely common small hatchback.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense, near-complete coverage across the peninsula — one of the best-covered parts of Southeast Asia.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Malacca Strait coastline, similar rainforest and oil palm plantations, both drive on the left
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Malaysian plates split into TWO white sections vs. Indonesia's three; Malaysian black-and-white kerbs and Perodua/Proton cars are strong tells; the black pole sticker also marks Peninsular Malaysia.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The peninsula uses black pole stickers and numeric federal route codes; Borneo uses white pole stickers (in Sarawak) and Sabah's 'A'-prefixed route codes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared peninsula, similar rubber/palm plantation landscape, both drive on the left
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Malaysian Latin-script signage and mosques vs. Thai script and Buddhist temples.
